newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Avonmore gives Waterford 2 for 1 share swap.
newsitem.headline: Avonmore gives Waterford 2 for 1 share swap.

text.p: Avonmore Foods Plc formally made an offer for Waterford Foods Plc on Monday, offering a two for one share swap for the group.

Avonmore, who made an initial approach for Waterford on Friday, said in a statement on Monday that it proposed to give one Avonmore share for every two Waterford Foods A and Waterford B ordinary shares.
Waterford said in a separate statement that it was considering the approach and a further announcement would be made in due course.
Based on closing prices on Friday the offer is worth about 290 million Irish pounds.
Avonmore is offering a further 68 million Irish pounds for preference shares and about 36 million Irish pounds in bonuses to farmers via milk prices.
If Avonmore succeeds, the combined turnover of the new group will be in excess of 2.5 billion Irish pounds.

Analysts said the synergies between the two companies were considerable and would create major economies of scale and opportunities for rationalisation since both were involved in the dairy industry and in trading animal feeds and fertilisers.
Avonmore's chances of succeeding after failing in a similar attempt in 1991 were greatly enhanced by the fact that Waterford had had a very tough year.
Waterford's profits and share price have plummeted as its margins were squeezed by lower butter and milk prices amid internal wrangling and a serious shake-up in its management structure.
Avonmore said the Waterford creamery milk price would be brought into line with the Avonmore price on completion of the merger. It estimated the present differential at 3.25 pence per gallon.
The combined Avonmore Waterford Group Plc board would comprise 19 Avonmore farmers and 11 representatives from Waterford, it said.
One of the farmer members from Avonmore would be chairman of Avonmore Waterford Co-Op Ltd and Avonmore Waterford Group Plc, and one of the farmer members from Waterford would be vice chairman.
